title: Keeping track of client billings and invoices
overviewCopy: Billable time gets lost in the gaps between doing the work and writing it down — an email answered on the train, a five-minute call between hearings. PointOne reads your time entries, correspondence and calendar to draft the billing lines you'd otherwise forget, so nothing goes unbilled. A person still reviews and approves every line before a client ever sees an invoice.

videoScript.narration: Billable time has a habit of disappearing in the gaps — the email you answered on the train, the five-minute call between hearings, or the quick read-through of a filing before you forwarded it on.
videoScript.visualIntent: Icons representing emails, phone calls, and calendar events scatter off a daily timeline graphic to illustrate uncaptured time.

videoScript.narration: PointOne reads your time entries, correspondence, and calendar metadata, pulling that scattered activity into draft invoice lines automatically without guessing at what happened.
videoScript.visualIntent: A conceptual flowchart shows data streams from inbox and calendar icons consolidating into organized line-item cards.

videoScript.narration: Here is how activity metadata is organized directly into draft lines for review.
Nothing goes out to a client automatically. Every line PointOne drafts sits in a review queue where you check and adjust it — a firm policy step that should never be skipped for speed.
videoScript.visualIntent: A conceptual diagram shows draft items stopping at a mandatory human checkpoint icon before flowing into a final client invoice container.

videoScript.narration: Most firms find PointOne catches more billable time than manual logging alone, simply because it doesn't rely on remembering everything at the end of a long day.
videoScript.visualIntent: A simple bar chart animation compares standard manual time logging against comprehensive automated capture.
